sentences.text: The claimant is in appeal seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the II Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT at Kalaburagi (for short 'Tribunal') in MVC No.252/2014, vide judgment and award dated 13.06.2018.

entities.text: II Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT at Kalaburagi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The claimant, aged about 16 years suffered injuries when she was travelling to school in an autorickshaw bearing registration No.KA-32/A-8991.
She filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation from the owner and insurer of the autorickshaw.

The claim petition was contested by the insurer of the autorickshaw, who claimed that the driver of the autorickshaw was not possessing valid licence and therefore, it was not liable to indemnify the owner.
4. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
The father of the claimant was examined as PW.1 and he marked Exs.P1 to P11.
A doctor was examined as PW.2, who deposed that the claimant had suffered disability to the extent of 26% to the whole body.

The insurer examined one of its officials as RW.1 and marked Exs.R1 to R4.
5.
Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the accident and injuries suffered by the claimant were due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the autorickshaw.

It held that the claimant had suffered fracture of proximal part of left femur and that she was admitted Surekha D/O Vaijanath vs Mallikarjun And Ors on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147769817/
2 at District Hospital, Kalaburagi from 07.01.2014 to 30.01.2014.

sentences.text:
It considered the disability NC:
2023:KHC-K:1271 suffered by the claimant at 9% to the whole body and awarded the following compensation:
Pain suffered already and to be suffered Rs.1,00,000/- in future, mental and physical shock, hardship in convenience and discomfort Attendant charges, food and conveyance Rs.11,000/- charges Loss of amenities and nutrition food Rs.10,000/-
. The Tribunal directed the insurer of the autorickshaw to pay the compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.
Being aggrieved by the same, the present appeal is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of compensation.

7. The learned counsel for the appellant/claimant submitted that the claimant had suffered fracture of proximal part of left femur and that the disability as deposed by PW.2 was 26% to the whole body and the Tribunal had considered the same at 9%
mechanically.
She submits that the claimant is a school going child and due to the accident, she suffered a fracture which was NC: 2023:KHC-K:1271 treated by using implants which had to be removed.

Therefore,
the Tribunal must have awarded future medical expenses.

Therefore, she contends that in view of the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of MASTER MALLIKARJUN VS. DIVISIONAL MANAGER, NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED reported in (2014) 14 SCC 396 , the compensation has to be reworked.

entities.text: MASTER MALLIKARJUN VS. DIVISIONAL MANAGER, NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED reported in (2014) 14 SCC 396
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/insurer contended that PW.2 had deposed that the claimant had suffered disability to the extent of 26% to the whole body and therefore, 1/3rd of the same was considered and proper compensation was awarded.
She therefore prayed that the compensation awarded be not enhanced.
9. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the appellant/claimant as well as the learned counsel for the respondent/insurer.
The accident involving the autorickshaw is not in dispute.
It is also not in dispute that the claimant had suffered injuries in the accident.
PW.2 deposed that the claimant had suffered fracture of proximal part of left femur.

sentences.text: 3 disability suffered by her must have been considered and therefore, the Tribunal must have assessed the disability at 10% to the whole body taking into account the evidence of PW.2 that the claimant had suffered disability to the extent of 26% to the whole body.

Consequently, the claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation as follows:
Pain and suffering Rs.3,00,000/-
Inconvenience caused to parents Rs.16,000/-
Loss of future amenities Rs.16,000/-
Conveyance, food, nourishment Rs.10,000/-
expenses Future medical expenses Rs.10,000/-
Total Rs.3,52,000/-
 NC: 2023:KHC-K:1271 11.

In view of the above, the appeal is allowed in part and the compensation of Rs1,21,000/-
determined by the Tribunal is enhanced to a sum of Rs.3,52,000/-.
The enhanced compensation of Rs.2,31,000/- shall be paid by the insurer to the claimant along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.

The enhanced compensation amount along with interest shall be deposited by the insurer before the Tribunal within a period of one month from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment and award.
Upon deposit, 50% of the enhanced compensation and interest shall be deposited in the name of the claimant in any nationalized Bank for a period of 5 years.
